To bring AlphaClaw to life, Proxima Fusion engineers worked side by side with Google technical specialists over a four-week project. Operating as a single team, they ran daily standups to align their goals and held a dedicated hackathon at the Google Munich office. Today, the resulting agent operates natively right where the engineering team works—inside their Slack workspace—enabling physicists to instantly run and analyze simulations.

Because the agent operates directly on internal engineering systems, monitoring for safety and security issues, like leaking intellectual property or compromising data, is essential. Proxima Fusion used Gemini to build a secondary, independent reviewer agent on the platform. This model acts as a built-in safeguard, inspecting every command the agent intends to execute. If an action looks unfamiliar or attempts to alter a critical database, the reviewer agent pauses the run and messages a human engineer in Slack for explicit approval, ensuring researchers maintain complete control over the design loop.
